jsonld.description: The full English condensed into a single dish that bakes itself: beans and tomatoes simmered into a thick, savoury base, eggs cracked over, and the whole pan finished in the oven until the whites set and the yolks stay molten. It is the café's beans-on-toast and the Mediterranean shakshuka meeting in the middle, and the result is the coziest 30-minute breakfast in the British canon — one pan, eaten with toasted, buttered bread straight from the board. The technique worth learning is the base's reduction: the beans must thicken before the eggs go in, or their liquid floods the whites and leaves them ragged. Ten minutes of simmering turns the tin into a sauce — and the eggs poach in it rather than drowning.

skeleton:
Baked Eggs with Beans and Tomatoes

British · Easy · Serves 2

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English condensed into a single dish that bakes itself: beans and tomatoes simmered into a thick, savoury base, eggs cracked over, and the whole pan finished in the oven until the whites set and the yolks stay molten. It is the café's beans-on-toast and the Mediterranean shakshuka meeting in the middle, and the result is the coziest 30-minute breakfast in the British canon — one pan, eaten with toasted, buttered bread straight from the board. The technique worth learning is the base's reduction: the beans must thicken before the eggs go in, or their liquid floods the whites and leaves them ragged. Ten minutes of simmering turns the tin into a sauce — and the eggs poach in it rather than drowning.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The base

The eggs and finish

- **Use a pan that can go from hob to oven** — cast iron, stainless, or a flameproof ceramic dish, about 24 cm across. The base simmers on the hob; the eggs finish above it. If no such pan exists, simmer in a saucepan and pour into a buttered baking dish before the eggs. - **Drain tinned plum tomatoes well** — excess juice is the enemy of the thick base. - Warm the bread in a low oven (about 120 °C) while the dish bakes; it arrives crisp as the eggs land.

Baked Eggs with Beans and Tomatoes

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 20 minutes · Total: 30 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The base

  • 15 ml / 14 g olive oil
  • 1 small onion (100 g), finely diced
  • 1 garlic clove, sliced
  • 400 g baked beans (1 tin), or 300 g the homemade British-style baked beans
  • 200 g cherry tomatoes (about 16), halved, or 1 tin plum tomatoes (400 g), drained and crushed
  • 2 tsp (10 g) tomato purée
  • 5 ml mushroom ketchup or Worcestershire sauce
  • 2 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g smoked paprika
  • A pinch of chilli flakes (0.5 g), optional

The eggs and finish

  • 4 large eggs (220 g)
  • 30 g mature Cheddar or 40 g feta, crumbled (optional)
  • 10 g fresh parsley or chives, chopped
  • 4 slices (200 g) thick bread, toasted and buttered, or torn sourdough for dipping

Instructions

  1. **Build the base, 12–15 minutes.** Warm the oil in the pan over medium heat and soften the onion 6–7 minutes until translucent and beginning to colour at the edges. Add the garlic and paprika (and chilli if using) for 1 minute, then the tomato purée, beans, tomatoes, mushroom ketchup, and salt. Simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is thick enough that a spoon dragged through leaves a trail that holds for 3 seconds. Checkpoint — the base mounds on a spoon, the tomatoes have collapsed into the beans, and the pan's edge shows a slow, thick bubble — not a watery slosh. This thickness is what the eggs need; a wet base makes ragged whites.
  2. **The eggs and the bake, 8–10 minutes at 190 °C.** Take the pan off the heat. Make 4 wells in the base with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Scatter the cheese between them if using. Bake 8–10 minutes, until the whites are just opaque and set and the yolks still dome and tremble. Checkpoint — the whites are set but custard-soft (they firm further in the first minute out), the yolks wobble when the pan is nudged. Pull them at the first full set — the carryover is real.
  3. **Finish and serve in the pan.** Scatter the herbs, bring the pan to the table on a board, and serve with the hot buttered toast for scooping and dipping. Checkpoint — the eating test: toast dragged through yolk, then base, in one dip — the dish's whole point.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Whites ragged and streaky into the baseBase too thinThe full 8–10 minute reduction; the trail-holding spoon test is the gate
Yolks hard by servingOverbaked or rested too longPull at first set — custard whites, trembling yolks; the pan finishes them
Base tastes flatTimid seasoningMushroom ketchup and salt up; beans are sweet and need savoury depth
Eggs spread across the whole panNo wells madeThe spoon-wells cradle each egg and keep whites contained

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **The base keeps 4 days refrigerated** and improves — make double, and future breakfasts are a 10-minute eggs-and-bake. Freeze the base 2 months. The eggs are always cracked fresh. - **Variation — the black pudding version:** 100 g black pudding, diced and crisped in the oil before the onion, makes it a full English in one pan — the meat slot filled. - **Variation — the bubble version:** a layer of leftover bubble and squeak pressed into the pan's base, the bean mixture over, eggs on top — the left-over refrigerator's finest hour. - **Serving math:** one 24 cm pan serves 2 with toast; two pans serve 4 and bake side by side.
